question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Be like chalk and cheese
option_1: To be completely different from each other
option_2: To be very similar to each other
option_3: To have a close relation with another person
option_4: To be distantly related to each other
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To be completely different from each other.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(to be) like chalk and cheese" is used for two persons or things that are utterly unlike each other, even though they may look similar at first glance. (एक-दूसरे से बिल्कुल भिन्न होना)

◦ Example: The two brothers are like chalk and cheese — one is a shy bookworm, the other a noisy sportsman.

• The image behind the idiom: chalk and cheese can look alike (both white, both crumbly blocks) but are completely different in nature and use — hence the sense of total dissimilarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To be very similar to each other" is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning — it is the trap option for candidates who guess from the "look-alike" image.

• Option 3 "To have a close relation with another person" and Option 4 "To be distantly related to each other" wrongly interpret the idiom as being about kinship/relationship, whereas it is about difference in nature, character or quality.

NOTE

• Idioms with a similar sense of difference: "poles apart", "a world of difference", "different as night and day", "not in the same league".

• Idioms with the opposite sense (similarity): "two peas in a pod", "birds of a feather", "cut from the same cloth", "spitting image".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Everyone liked the lively music being played at the restaurant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sombre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lively" (adjective) means full of life and energy; spirited, animated, cheerful. (जीवंत / उल्लासपूर्ण)

• "Sombre" means dark, gloomy, dull and serious in mood or colour — the exact antonym of lively. (उदास / गमगीन)

◦ Correct: Lively music raises the spirits, while sombre music creates a heavy, mournful mood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Durable" means long-lasting/hard-wearing — it is unrelated to mood or energy.

• Option 2 "Cheerful" (happy, bright) is a synonym of lively, not its antonym — a classic distractor.

• Option 3 "Speedy" means fast; speed is not the same as liveliness of spirit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lively: animated, vivacious, energetic, spirited, buoyant, sprightly, exuberant.

• Antonyms of lively: sombre, dull, lifeless, listless, lethargic, gloomy, subdued.

• Note the British spelling "sombre" (American: "somber").

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Fourty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fourty" is misspelt. The correct spelling of the number 40 is "forty" — without the "u". (चालीस)

◦ Correct: There were forty students in the classroom.

• Remember the rule: four → fourteen (with u), but four → forty (no u). English keeps the "u" in four and fourteen but drops it in forty.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Committee" (a group of people appointed for a function) is correctly spelt — it has a double m, double t and double e (CO-M-M-I-T-T-E-E).

• "Hypnotic" (inducing sleep or a trance-like state) is correctly spelt.

• "Tennessee" (a state of the USA) is correctly spelt — double n, double s, double e.

NOTE

• Other frequently misspelt number words: ninth (not "nineth"), ninety (not "ninty"), eighth (not "eightth"), twelfth (not "twelth").

• Commonly tested spellings in SSC: accommodation, occurrence, embarrass, harass, maintenance, questionnaire, privilege, separate.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined segment in the following sentence.

Raymond has opted the study of religion as his major subject in graduation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Theology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Theology" is the study of religion, God and religious belief. (धर्मशास्त्र / धर्म का अध्ययन)

◦ Correct: Raymond has opted theology as his major subject in graduation.

• Word roots: Greek theos = god + logia = study of ⇒ theology = study of God/religion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Psephology" is the study of elections and voting trends/statistics. (चुनाव विज्ञान)

• Option 2 "Philology" is the study of the history and development of languages, especially of literary texts. (भाषा-विज्ञान)

• Option 4 "Psychology" is the study of the human mind and behaviour. (मनोविज्ञान)

NOTE

• Other "-logy" one-word substitutes for SSC: Etymology (study of word origins), Entomology (study of insects), Ornithology (study of birds), Anthropology (study of human beings and societies), Numismatics (study of coins), Epigraphy (study of inscriptions), Seismology (study of earthquakes), Cardiology (study of the heart).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom from the given options to fill in the blank.

Greta Thunberg _____________ when she dared to question about accountability with respect to global warming and climate change.
option_4: hit the nail on the head
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hit the nail on the head.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hit the nail on the head" means to describe or identify exactly what is causing a problem; to say precisely the right thing. (सटीक बात कहना / ठीक निशाने पर बात करना)

◦ Correct: Greta Thunberg hit the nail on the head when she dared to question about accountability with respect to global warming and climate change.

• The sentence praises her for raising precisely the right issue (accountability), so this idiom fits perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sow wild oats" means to lead a wild, pleasure-seeking life when young — irrelevant here.

• Option 2 "keep the pot boiling" means to keep something going/maintain interest, or to earn just enough to live — it does not convey accuracy of statement.

• Option 3 "give the devil his due" means to acknowledge the good qualities of a person one dislikes — it does not fit the context.

NOTE

• Idioms of precision/correctness: "hit the bull's eye", "hit the mark", "on the money", "spot on".

• Greta Thunberg is a Swedish climate activist who began the "Fridays for Future" school-strike movement — useful context for current-affairs based English passages.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

When Rajesh was going to college, he meet with an accident.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. met.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subordinate clause "When Rajesh was going to college" is in the past continuous tense, which fixes the sentence in the past. The main clause must therefore take the simple past — "met" (meet – met – met).

◦ Correct: When Rajesh was going to college, he met with an accident.

• Rule: when a shorter action interrupts a longer ongoing past action, the longer action takes the past continuous and the interrupting action takes the simple past.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "has met" is the present perfect, which cannot be used with a clearly past time frame set by "was going".

• Option 2 "meets" is the simple present and clashes with the past context.

• Option 4 "No substitution required" is wrong because "he meet" is a plain subject-verb/tense error — the base form "meet" cannot stand as a finite past verb with the singular subject "he".

NOTE

• "Meet with an accident" is the standard Indian-English collocation for to have an accident.

• Similar structure: "While she was cooking, the phone rang." / "When I was walking home, it started to rain."

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

As soon as I shall win the lottery, I hope to buy a Ferrari.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shall win.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a clause of time introduced by conjunctions such as as soon as, when, till, until, before, after, by the time, the future tense is never used. The simple present is used instead to express future meaning.

◦ Incorrect: As soon as I shall win the lottery, I hope to buy a Ferrari.

◦ Correct: As soon as I win the lottery, I hope to buy a Ferrari.

• So the erroneous underlined part is "shall win", which should be "win".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "As soon as" is the correct conjunction for two closely following events — no error.

• Option 1 "hope" is a stative verb correctly used in the simple present in the main clause — no error.

• Option 4 "a Ferrari" correctly uses the article "a" before a consonant sound /f/ — no error.

NOTE

• The same rule applies to conditional clauses with "if": "If it rains (not will rain), we will cancel the match."

• Time/condition clause ⇒ present tense; main clause ⇒ future tense. Example: "I will call you when I reach home."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Some things are meant to be, and death is ______ for humans.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. natural.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Natural" means existing in or caused by nature; normal and to be expected. The first half of the sentence — "Some things are meant to be" — expresses inevitability, so death being "natural" for humans is the logical completion. (स्वाभाविक / प्राकृतिक)

◦ Correct: Some things are meant to be, and death is natural for humans.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "edible" means fit to be eaten — nonsensical here.

• Option 2 "spiral" means shaped like a coil (or a continuous downward movement) — it does not describe death for humans.

• Option 4 "viral" means caused by a virus, or spreading rapidly online — death in general is not viral.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with natural: natural death, natural resources, natural disaster, natural instinct, natural selection.

• Synonyms of natural (in this sense): normal, usual, inevitable, ordinary, expected. Antonyms: unnatural, artificial, abnormal.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

They complained that their manager was incompietent and knew nothing about the project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. incompetent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "incompietent" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "incompetent", meaning not having the necessary skill or ability to do something successfully. (अक्षम / अयोग्य)

◦ Correct: They complained that their manager was incompetent and knew nothing about the project.

• Spelling key: IN + COM + PE + TENT — there is no letter "i" after "comp".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "incompitent" wrongly writes "i" in place of the second "e".

• Option 2 "incompeteant" wrongly inserts an extra "a".

• Option 3 "incomepetent" wrongly inserts an "e" after "incom".

NOTE

• Word family: competent (able, skilled) → competence/competency (noun) → incompetent (adjective) → incompetence (noun).

• The prefix "in-" here means "not" — as in inefficient, inadequate, incapable, inaccurate.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Distinguished
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Dignified.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Distinguished" (adjective) means highly respected, eminent, of noble and impressive appearance or achievement. (प्रतिष्ठित / गरिमामय)

• "Dignified" means having or showing a composed, serious and worthy manner; commanding respect — the closest synonym. (गरिमापूर्ण)

◦ Example: The distinguished/dignified professor was honoured at the convocation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mirrored" means reflected — it relates to reflection, not to eminence.

• Option 3 "Dramatic" means striking, theatrical or sudden — it describes effect, not respectability.

• Option 4 "Mediocre" means of only average or poor quality — this is an antonym of distinguished.

NOTE

• Synonyms of distinguished: eminent, illustrious, renowned, celebrated, esteemed, dignified, august, noted.

• Antonyms: mediocre, ordinary, undistinguished, unknown, obscure.

• Note the second sense of "distinguished" — the past participle of distinguish (to tell apart): "He distinguished between the two theories."

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Periodic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Irregular.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Periodic" means occurring or recurring at regular intervals. (नियतकालिक / नियमित अंतराल पर होने वाला)

• "Irregular" means not occurring at even or regular intervals; uneven, erratic — the exact antonym of periodic. (अनियमित)

◦ Example: Periodic health check-ups are done at fixed intervals, whereas irregular visits follow no fixed pattern.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Holistic" means dealing with the whole rather than the parts — unrelated to time intervals.

• Option 2 "Dynamic" means full of energy and constantly changing — it is not the opposite of "regular in occurrence".

• Option 4 "Tedious" means boring and tiresome — it describes quality, not frequency.

NOTE

• Synonyms of periodic: recurrent, cyclical, intermittent, regular, seasonal, sporadic (loosely).

• Antonyms: irregular, constant, continuous, unremitting, erratic.

• Related: the "Periodic Table" is so named because chemical properties recur at regular intervals of atomic number.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Manisha saw an old elephant / in the wildlife reserve / while she was / on safari tour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. on safari tour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A singular countable noun ("tour") must be preceded by a determiner. The correct phrase is "on a safari tour" (or "on safari"), not "on safari tour".

◦ Incorrect: ... while she was on safari tour.

◦ Correct: ... while she was on a safari tour.

• So the segment containing the error is the fourth one, given as Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Manisha saw an old elephant" is correct — "an" is rightly used before the vowel sound in "old".

• "in the wildlife reserve" is correct — "the" is used for a particular, identified reserve.

• "while she was" correctly introduces a clause of time in the past.

NOTE

• Articles with singular countable nouns are compulsory: "He is a doctor", "She bought a car", "They went on a picnic/a trip/a tour."

• Note the fixed expressions without an article: "on safari", "on holiday", "at school", "in hospital" (British usage).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

In Nepal, the food is more cheaper than in Sri Lanka.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. more cheaper.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "More cheaper" is a double comparative, which is always incorrect in English. The adjective "cheap" is a one-syllable word, so its comparative is formed by adding "-er" ⇒ "cheaper". Adding "more" as well is redundant.

◦ Incorrect: In Nepal, the food is more cheaper than in Sri Lanka.

◦ Correct: In Nepal, the food is cheaper than in Sri Lanka.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "the food is" is correct — "food" is an uncountable noun taking a singular verb.

• "than in Sri Lanka" correctly completes the comparison.

• "In Nepal" is a correct prepositional phrase of place.

NOTE

• Rule of degrees: short adjectives take -er/-est (tall–taller–tallest; cheap–cheaper–cheapest); long adjectives take more/most (beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful).

• Never combine the two: "more better", "most easiest", "more worse" are all wrong.

• Adjectives with irregular degrees: good–better–best, bad–worse–worst, little–less–least, much/many–more–most.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Most times, he is sitting alone, immersed in his own ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. monologue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "monologue" is a long speech made by one person, or a person's inner speech/thinking to oneself. Someone "sitting alone, immersed in his own monologue" is absorbed in talking to himself or in his own train of thought. (स्वगत कथन / एकालाप)

◦ Correct: Most times, he is sitting alone, immersed in his own monologue.

• Roots: Greek monos = one/single + logos = speech ⇒ speech by one person.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Synagogue" is a Jewish place of worship — it is a building, not something one can be immersed in as a thought.

• Option 3 "Mystagogue" is a teacher/initiator into mystical doctrines — a person, so it cannot be "his own".

• Option 4 "Prologue" is the introductory part of a play, book or speech — it does not fit a person sitting alone thinking.

NOTE

• Related literary terms: dialogue (conversation between two or more), soliloquy (a character speaking thoughts aloud, alone on stage — e.g. Hamlet's "To be, or not to be"), epilogue (concluding section), prologue (opening section).

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options.

He has neither the policies nor the persanol charisma to inspire people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. personal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence, the incorrectly spelt word is "persanol". Its correct spelling is "personal", meaning belonging to or affecting a particular person; individual. (व्यक्तिगत)

◦ Correct: He has neither the policies nor the personal charisma to inspire people.

• Spelling key: PER + SON + AL (from "person" + "-al").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other three options are themselves misspellings of words that are already correct in the sentence:

◦ "cherisma" → the correct spelling is "charisma" (compelling personal charm), which is already correct in the sentence.

◦ "polecies" → the correct spelling is "policies", already correct in the sentence.

◦ "niether" → the correct spelling is "neither", already correct in the sentence.

NOTE

• Do not confuse personal (private, individual) with personnel (the staff/employees of an organisation): "Personal problems should not affect work" vs "The personnel department handles recruitment."

• The "neither ... nor" correlative pair used in the sentence is correct; remember "either ... or", "neither ... nor", "both ... and".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The judge wanted to hear straight from the horse’s mouth.
option_3: In close vicinity to the juror
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Directly from the person involved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "straight from the horse's mouth" means directly from the original, most reliable or authoritative source — i.e., from the person actually involved. (प्रत्यक्ष / विश्वसनीय स्रोत से)

◦ Correct: The judge wanted to hear straight from the horse's mouth — that is, from the person directly concerned, not through others.

• Origin: in horse racing, the most trustworthy tip about a horse would come from the horse itself; buyers also judge a horse's age by examining its teeth (its mouth).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Directly from the lawyer" is too narrow — the idiom is not about lawyers at all.

• Option 3 "In close vicinity to the juror" confuses the idiom with physical nearness.

• Option 4 "Having ears which never fail" is unrelated to the idea of a reliable source.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "first-hand information", "from the source", "get it straight".

• Opposite sense: "hearsay", "a little bird told me", "through the grapevine" (rumour/indirect information).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Virtual reality is the creation of a virtual environment presented to our senses in such a way that we experience it as if we were really there.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part "presented to our senses" is a reduced passive relative clause — it is short for "which is presented to our senses". The environment receives the action (it is presented), so the past participle (V3) "presented" is correct.

◦ Correct as printed: ... a virtual environment presented to our senses in such a way that we experience it as if we were really there.

• The preposition "to" is right: something is presented to somebody/something.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "presenting to our senses" wrongly uses the present participle (V-ing), which would make the environment the doer of the action.

• Option 2 "presenting in our senses" is doubly wrong — wrong participle and wrong preposition ("in" instead of "to").

• Option 3 "presents to our senses" would create two finite verbs ("is" and "presents") in the same clause without a connector.

NOTE

• Reduced relative clauses: "the book (which was) written by Tagore", "the man (who was) injured in the crash" — use V3 for passive sense and V-ing for active sense: "the man standing at the gate".

• Note also the correct subjunctive "as if we were really there" (unreal comparison uses "were" for all subjects).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom from the given options to fill in the blank.

Being a journalist, your first duty is to ____________ or else your colleagues might surpass you.
option_4: keep your ear to the ground
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. keep your ear to the ground.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "keep one's ear to the ground" means to stay well informed about what is happening; to be alert to news, trends and opinions. (हर हलचल की जानकारी रखना / सतर्क रहना)

◦ Correct: Being a journalist, your first duty is to keep your ear to the ground or else your colleagues might surpass you.

• This is exactly the duty of a journalist — to remain alert to developments, otherwise rivals will get the story first.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "eat a humble pie" means to admit one's mistake and apologise humbly — it does not fit "first duty" of a journalist.

• Option 2 "have an axe to grind" means to have a private, selfish motive for doing something.

• Option 3 "build castles in the air" means to make impractical, day-dreaming plans.

NOTE

• Idioms of alertness/awareness: "keep one's eyes peeled/skinned", "keep tabs on", "be on the ball", "keep abreast of".

• The origin of "ear to the ground" is often traced to trackers/scouts who literally listened at the ground for approaching hoofbeats.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) He will come / (B) and receive you / (C) at the station / (D) when you will arrive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. D.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (D) "when you will arrive" contains the error. In a clause of time introduced by when, before, after, until, till, as soon as, the future tense is not used; the simple present conveys future meaning.

◦ Incorrect: He will come and receive you at the station when you will arrive.

◦ Correct: He will come and receive you at the station when you arrive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Part (A) "He will come" is correct — the main clause rightly takes the future tense.

• Part (B) "and receive you" is correct — "receive" is correctly in the base form after "will come and".

• Part (C) "at the station" is a correct prepositional phrase ("at" is used for a specific point/place such as a station).

NOTE

• The same restriction applies to if-clauses (conditional type 1): "If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home." — never "if it will rain".

• Summary: subordinate clause of time/condition ⇒ present tense; main clause ⇒ future tense.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She is very good / in playing / the guitar / and singing songs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. in playing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "good" takes the preposition "at" when it refers to skill or ability, not "in".

◦ Incorrect: She is very good in playing the guitar and singing songs.

◦ Correct: She is very good at playing the guitar and singing songs.

• So the erroneous segment is the second one, given as Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "She is very good" is correct — "very" properly modifies the adjective "good".

• "the guitar" is correct — names of musical instruments take the definite article "the" (play the guitar, the piano, the flute, the sitar).

• "and singing songs" is correct — the gerund "singing" is parallel with "playing".

NOTE

• Adjective + preposition combinations frequently tested in SSC: good at, bad at, expert in/at, proficient in, capable of, fond of, afraid of, interested in, jealous of, angry with (a person)/at (a thing), superior to, inferior to, married to.

• Note also: we say "play the guitar" (instrument) but "play _____ cricket" (game, no article).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. concern.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "concern" (noun) means a matter of worry or anxiety; something that causes people to be troubled. (चिंता का विषय)

• The clause that follows — "as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems" — clearly signals worry, so pollution is a growing concern.

◦ Correct: Environmental pollution is a growing concern all around the world ...

• The collocation "a growing concern" is standard English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "interest" suggests curiosity or attraction, not risk or worry.

• Option 2 "duty" means an obligation — pollution is not an obligation.

• Option 4 "charge" means an accusation, a fee or responsibility — it does not fit "a growing ____ ... as it poses significant risks".

NOTE

• Useful collocations: "cause for concern", "a matter of grave concern", "growing concern", "of great concern".

• Synonyms of concern (worry): anxiety, apprehension, disquiet, unease, worry.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sources.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb that follows the blank is "vary" — a plural verb form. Therefore the subject must be plural: "The sources ... vary from natural causes ... to human actions."

◦ Correct: The sources of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions ...

• Meaning-wise, "sources" = the origins or causes from which pollution comes, which suits "vary from ... to ...".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "source" is singular and would require "varies", not "vary" — subject-verb disagreement.

• Option 1 "sourcing" (the act of obtaining supplies) and Option 3 "sourced" (past participle) are not nouns that fit the slot after "The" and before "of environmental pollution vary".

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement rule: the verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, not with the noun in the intervening prepositional phrase. Here the head noun is "sources" (plural), not "pollution".

• Example: "The causes of the accident are still unknown." / "The list of items is on the table."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. As a result.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "of these activities". Only "As a result" combines with "of" to form the fixed phrase "as a result of", meaning because of / as a consequence of. (के परिणामस्वरूप)

◦ Correct: As a result of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil ...

• The sentence states the consequence of the human activities listed in the previous sentence, so a cause-effect connector is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Since" (meaning "because") introduces a clause with a subject and verb, not a noun phrase — "Since these activities happen" would be needed.

• Option 2 "However" shows contrast, which breaks the logical flow.

• Option 4 "Therefore" is not followed by "of"; it is used as "Therefore, pollutants are released ..." — grammatically wrong before "of these activities".

NOTE

• Connectors of result: as a result of, because of, owing to, due to, on account of, consequently, hence, thus, therefore.

• Remember: "due to / owing to / because of / as a result of" are followed by a noun/noun phrase; "because / since / as" are followed by a clause.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. and.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence lists two similar causes of environmental pollution — (i) "human attitudes towards sustainability" and (ii) "their lack of environmental awareness". Two like items in a list are joined by the coordinating conjunction "and".

◦ Correct: One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability and their lack of environmental awareness.

• Note that both items are noun phrases, so only a coordinating conjunction can join them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "since" and 4 "because" are subordinating conjunctions of reason and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb), not by the noun phrase "their lack of environmental awareness".

• Option 3 "but" shows contrast; the two causes here are complementary, not contrasting.

NOTE

• Coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS): For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So — they join elements of equal grammatical rank.

• Keep parallel structure when using "and": "human attitudes ... and their lack of ..." — both noun phrases.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. like.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank must introduce examples of "individual choices". The preposition "like" means "such as" and can be directly followed by a noun/gerund: "choices like driving or using single-use plastics". (जैसे कि)

◦ Correct: Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices like driving or using single-use plastics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "example" and Option 4 "instance" are nouns; they would need supporting words — "for example" / "for instance" — and are normally set off by commas, so the bare noun cannot fill the slot.

• Option 2 "while" is a conjunction of time/contrast and would need a clause, giving no sense here.

NOTE

• "Like" and "such as" both introduce examples: "fruits like/such as mangoes and apples".

• Do not confuse this "like" (preposition = similar to / for example) with the verb "like" (to enjoy). After the preposition "like", a verb takes the -ing (gerund) form — "like driving", "like using".
